summary: Guy Reid was jailed 5 years 9 months for a kidnapping in which the victim was held in a car boot for about five hours.
source_citation: SBS News, 'Vic kidnap victim thought she would die' (reported 2016); Guy Reid pleaded guilty to one count of kidnapping, victim held ~5 hours in car boot, jailed 5 yrs 9 mo. https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/vic-kidnap-victim-thought-she-would-die/liljppdn4

summary: Terence Darrell Kelly was sentenced to 13 years 6 months (plus an A$1,000 fine) for the 18-day forcible abduction of 4-year-old Cleo Smith in Western Australia.
source_citation: NBC News; Wikipedia 'Abduction of Cleo Smith'; held 16 Oct – 3 Nov 2021 (18 days); sentenced 5 Apr 2023 to 13 yrs 6 mo plus A$1,000 fine, parole after 11.5 yrs (A$1,000 ≈ USD 660 in 2024). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abduction_of_Cleo_Smith

summary: In R v Jacklin (1995) a forcible confinement of about two hours drew a 3-year sentence under Criminal Code s.279.
source_citation: Criminal Law Notebook, 'Kidnapping and Unlawful Confinement (Sentencing Cases)' digest; R v Jacklin (1995), ~2-hour confinement, 3 years imposed (s.279, max 10 yrs indictable). https://criminalnotebook.ca/index.php?title=Kidnapping_and_Unlawful_Confinement_(Sentencing_Cases)

summary: Canada's Criminal Code s.279(2) sets forcible confinement at up to 10 years (indictable) or 18 months (summary), with duration as an aggravating factor rather than a statutory threshold.
harm_duration: no numeric statutory threshold (duration aggravates at sentencing)
source_citation: Criminal Code of Canada s.279, Justice Canada; s.279(2) max 10 years indictable / 18 months summary; ceiling anchor for Canadian liberty pricing. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/c-46/section-279.html

summary: France's Code pénal art. 224-1 sets séquestration at 20 years' criminal detention, reduced to 5 years and a EUR 75,000 fine if the victim is voluntarily released before the seventh day.
harm_duration: before the 7th day vs 7th day or later (7-day cliff)
source_citation: Légifrance, Code pénal art. 224-1: basic 20 years réclusion criminelle; if released voluntarily before the 7th day, 5 years + EUR 75,000 fine (≈ USD 85,000 in 2024); aggravated to 30 years (permanent infirmity) or life (torture/death). https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000027811104

summary: Germany's §239 StGB (Freiheitsberaubung) sets a basic penalty of up to 5 years, rising to 1–10 years when the deprivation of liberty lasts longer than one week.
source_citation: gesetze-im-internet.de §239 StGB: Abs.(1) up to 5 years or fine; Abs.(3) Nr.1 (deprivation >1 week) 1–10 years; Abs.(4) (death results) not less than 3 years. https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/stgb/__239.html

summary: India's IPC s.343 punishes wrongful confinement for three days or more with up to 2 years' imprisonment.
source_citation: Indian Penal Code s.343 (confinement 'for three days, or more'), max 2 years; mirrored in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. https://lawrato.com/indian-kanoon/ipc/section-343

summary: India's IPC s.344 punishes wrongful confinement for ten days or more with up to 3 years' imprisonment.
source_citation: Indian Penal Code s.344 (confinement 'for ten days, or more'), max 3 years; mirrored in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. https://restthecase.com/knowledge-bank/ipc/section-344

summary: India's IPC s.365 (kidnapping/abduction with intent to confine) caps at 7 years and s.367 (to cause grievous hurt or slavery) caps at 10 years, with no duration threshold.
source_citation: Indian Penal Code s.365 (intent to confine) max 7 years; s.367 (to cause grievous hurt/slavery) max 10 years; intent-based ceiling anchors, not duration-keyed. https://lawrato.com/indian-kanoon/ipc/section-365

summary: England & Wales Kidnap/False Imprisonment guideline (effective 1 April 2025) sets Category 1A, where detention over a sustained period is a greatest-harm factor, at a starting point of 11 years' custody (range 8–16 years, max life).
harm_duration: sustained period (qualitative harm factor, no numeric threshold)
source_citation: Sentencing Council (England & Wales), 'Kidnap/False Imprisonment' guideline, effective 1 Apr 2025; Cat 1A starting point 11 years, range 8–16 years; 2023 mean custodial sentence 7 years 7 months. https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/kidnap-false-imprisonment/

summary: Phillip Garrido was sentenced to 431 years to life for the ~18-year kidnapping and rape of Jaycee Dugard.
source_citation: CNN/CBS News; Wikipedia 'Kidnapping of Jaycee Dugard'; abducted 10 Jun 1991, recovered 26 Aug 2009 (~18 years); sentenced 2 Jun 2011 to 431 years to life; co-defendant Nancy Garrido 36 years to life. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidnapping_of_Jaycee_Dugard

summary: Brian David Mitchell received life without parole for the ~9-month interstate kidnapping and captivity of 14-year-old Elizabeth Smart.
source_citation: FBI/DOJ press release, May 2011 (Brian David Mitchell sentencing); held 5 Jun 2002 – 12 Mar 2003 (~9 months); sentence: life without parole; co-defendant Wanda Barzee 15 years. https://archives.fbi.gov/archives/saltlakecity/press-releases/2011/slc052511a.htm

summary: Ariel Castro was sentenced to life plus 1,000 years without parole for holding three victims captive for roughly a decade each.
source_citation: CNN, 1 Aug 2013; Ariel Castro pleaded guilty to 937 counts; three victims held ~2002–2004 to 2013; sentence life + 1,000 years, no parole. https://www.cnn.com/2013/08/01/justice/ohio-castro
